}\n    }\n\n    // Pin the host output region so device-to-host copies are asynchronous.\n    void pinHost(double* ptr, size_t count) {\n        if (count == 0) return;\n        if {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgN5GPgZp8BbW6Noa4qEN","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA version is done, verified against the original, and only the two existing files were changed.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` now runs unconditionally as MPI + OpenMP + CUDA. The global option set is split into one contiguous chunk per MPI rank, and each rank binds to one GPU by local rank. Within a rank, a fixed share of the chunk is priced on the GPU and the rest on the CPU cores with OpenMP at the same time.\n- The GPU path generates inputs in-kernel from the option index with the same arithmetic as the host generator, so only the 8-byte price crosses PCIe. Work is tiled over four streams so kernels overlap the device-to-host copies into pinned host memory.\n- OpenMP also parallelizes host-side input generation. One OpenMP thread queues the GPU work and then joins the dynamically scheduled CPU loop.\n- Results are gathered to rank 0 only when needed for `-r` or `-v`, and rank 0 alone prints. Timing is the maximum across ranks after a barrier. All original flags, output formats, and exit codes are preserved.\n- `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt` compiles the single source as CUDA, links MPI, OpenMP, and the CUDA runtime, forwards the host flags through nvcc, and defaults to native GPU architectures. The executable is still `black_scholes`.\n\n**Verification** on this node (4 RTX 3090s, 2x 64-core EPYC):\n\n| Run | 10M options | 100M options | 1B options |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Original serial | 900 ms | | |\n| Hybrid, 4 ranks x 64 threads | 25 ms | 27 to 29 ms | 233 ms |\n\nPrices match the reference to within one or two ulps, which is the expected difference between the CUDA and glibc `erf`. Validation passes, and the sum, min, max, and samples agree with the serial output. The byte-exact FNV hash therefore differs from the serial run, as it would for any GPU port.\n\n**Things to know**\n\n- The GPU share defaults to 0.7 of each rank's chunk, which was the measured optimum here since the 3090's FP64 rate is modest and the kernel is compute-bound. The environment variable `BS_GPU_FRACTION` overrides it for nodes with a different CPU-to-GPU ratio. The split is fixed rather than dynamic so results are bit-reproducible across runs.\n- Run one rank per GPU. Open MPI binds jobs of one or two ranks to a single core by default, which starves the OpenMP threads, so launch with something like `--map-by numa --bind-to numa` or `--bind-to none`.
